keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -206..-203; no Cliopatria row. Hengshan under Wu Rui: 'eastern Hubei, Jiangxi'. The pages do not date the end of Hengshan; the Ying Bu page has Hengshan and Yuzhang under Ying Bu's Huainan from 203.

correction.text: Changsha: 'present-day Hunan and some surrounding areas'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -202..-157: 'present-day Hunan and some surrounding areas'; the Book of Han lists Changsha, Yuzhang, Xiang, Guilin and Nanhai, but Yuzhang had gone to Ying Bu and Xiang, Guilin and Nanhai were Zhao Tuo's; 'Wuling and Guiyang were actually controlled by Changsha'. Hunan stands for it. Cliopatria's Han shape includes Hunan throughout.

ledger.note: 206 BC: Wu Rui is King of Hengshan. Xiang Yu created the Eighteen Kingdoms in 206 BC; Hengshan, ruled by Wu Rui, covered 'eastern Hubei, Jiangxi' and 'allies with Liu Bang' (fate column). The Changsha page gives 'one year later' after 207, so 206 is the group's year.

203 BC: Hengshan and Yuzhang pass to Ying Bu. Ying Bu was instated King of Huainan in 203, ruling 'Jiujiang, Lushan, Hengshan and Yuzhang'; the Changsha page: Yuzhang 'had already gone to Ying Bu'. Month unknown.

202 BC: Wu Rui becomes King of Changsha. 'The kingdom was founded when Emperor Gaozu granted the territory to his follower Wu Rui in 203 or 202 BC'; Wu Rui's reign table reads 203-202 BC. Same king, same house; Hengshan to Changsha.

region.text: Changsha: 'present-day Hunan and some surrounding areas'

ledger.note: 202 BC: Changsha. Gaozu granted Wu Rui Changsha, 'present-day Hunan and some surrounding areas', with Wuling and Guiyang actually controlled; the page's 203 or 202 BC.

region.text: the border counties of southern Hunan that Zhao Tuo occupied

ledger.note: 183 BC: Zhao Tuo attacks Changsha. 'In 183 BC, however, Empress Lü banned the export of iron ware to Nanyue, which angered Zhao Tuo', who 'twice invaded Changsha, occupying a few counties'. The Changsha page dates the ban, not the invasions; 183 is the Nanyue page's first-antagonism start used by ea-02-c's nanyue dossier.

region.text: the border counties of southern Hunan that Zhao Tuo occupied

ledger.note: 179 BC: the antagonism ends. The Changsha page says the Han campaign was abandoned 'with the death of Empress Lü' without a year; 179 is the Nanyue dossier's end of the first antagonism. PAGE SILENT on the year.

ledger.note: 157 BC: the Wu line ends. 'Wu Zhu reigned for twenty-one years, dying in 157 BC without male issue'; 'In 155 BC, the kingdom was reestablished for a member of the imperial family' (Liu Fa, 155-128 BC).

notes: Changsha Kingdom (Hengshan -206..-203, Changsha -202..-157): the Wu family's Han vassal kingdom. 3 pages opened (Changsha Kingdom; Eighteen Kingdoms; Ying Bu). I merged the Hengshan of the Eighteen Kingdoms (flagged 'hengshan' by ea-02-b) with Changsha because Wu Rui is one man (rename event), but their lands differ (Hengshan eastern Hubei and Jiangxi, Changsha Hunan). The Liu-house Changsha (155 BC - AD 33, Liu Fa to Liu Xing) is not dossiered: it sits inside the Han shape and the page gives its end as the demotion of Liu Xing in AD 33. Unsettled: the end of Hengshan (the pages give none); Wu Rui's reign 203-202 against 202; the dates of Zhao Tuo's invasions (the page gives 183 for the embargo only). Counterparts: han-dynasty, nanyue, western-chu exist; huainan is written by this batch.
